pr_title: sql: attempt to unsplit ranges in GC job for secondary tenants
pr_body:
Previously, we did not attempt an AdminUnsplit for secondary tenants, since secondary tenants were incapable of issuing unsplit requests. With the addition of tenant capabilities, some tenants may be able to issue unsplits.

Now, we opportunistically issue unsplits in secondary tenants.  If the unsplit fails with a permissions error, we give up and move on.

Note that secondary tenants cannot scan the range descriptors directly, so we use the range iterator to find relevant ranges. As a result, we may miss some ranges if the range cache is out of date.

I've opted for a bit of code duplication to make it easier to verify during review that the non-MT code path, remains the same as before.

Fixes #116240

Release note: None

issue_context.title: multi-tenant: gcjob unsplit only supports system tenant
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Please describe the issue you observed, and any steps we can take to reproduce it:

**To Reproduce**

The GC Job has code to unsplit indexes and tables on drop, but that code does not run outside of the system tenant:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/7b66a50edf641514dc9366e53894ec5b6af2dd0f/pkg/sql/gcjob/gc_job.go#L203-L205

As a result, table's that have been manually split with long expirations may leave small empty ranges in the cluster for a long time as they will be unable to be merged.

Jira issue: CRDB-34536

review_comments: I could be convinced that we should never fail on an unsplit error here.

Random drive-by nit: I can understand the motivation to have a "split" capability, but I don't follow why we'd want to gate "unsplit" behind a capability.  Is there some way that "unsplit" would do anything but leave the cluster in a better (i.e. more efficient) state?  Of course, not something we'd need to resolve on this PR (either way), but something I've always wondered about.

I am having trouble reconstructing the entire conversation. But, I think at least part of the argument was that `split` is more dangerous than `unsplit` so you might want to allow `unsplit` while restricting `split` in response to some run-away tenant.

But, eh, I do kinda wonder if we would be better served by one capability. Especially since requests still can only impact ranges whose start key is inside the tenant's keyspace.
